Topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: Why Bouncing Blocks Count Digits of Pi

Target audience: High school students and undergraduate math enthusiasts

Section: section_1 — The Setup: The Elastic Collision Problem

Lecture lines:
Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
The wall collision reverses the small block.
Momentum and kinetic energy remain conserved.

Planned animations:
Create two blocks of masses m1 and m2 at #FFFFFF.
Animate m1 moving toward m2 with velocity v1.
Show collision of m1 and m2.
Show m1 rebounding and m2 moving forward.
Highlight collision forces with #FF0000 flash.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite: The Mapping to Velocity Space

Lecture lines:
Map velocities as coordinates on a plane.
Wall impacts look like reflections across axes.
Block collisions reflect across a constant line.

Planned animations:
Draw two circles in velocity space representing momentum conservation.
Display velocity vector v1 for block m1.
Represent mass ratio as circle radius ratio.

Section: section_3 — The Geometric Connection

Lecture lines:
The mass ratio determines the wedge angle.
Increasing mass makes the wedge very narrow.
Reflections bounce back and forth inside.
The number of bounces measures the arc.
It behaves like a bouncing billiard ball.

Planned animations:
Visualize billiard path as a reflection inside a circle.
Show billiard hitting walls at specific angles.
Label geometry as #00FF00 lines.

Section: section_4 — The Grand Reveal: Digits of Pi

Lecture lines:
Mass ratios of 100, 10,000, 1,000,000.
Collision counts follow digits of Pi.
Three, thirty-one, three hundred fourteen.
Conservation laws naturally encode the constant Pi.
Physics counting computes the circle's arc.

Planned animations:
Display digits of Pi appearing from billiard collisions.
Connect number of collisions to digits.
Highlight calculated digit with #FFFF00.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Intuition

Lecture lines:
Counting collisions is measuring an angle.
Discrete bounces approximate the circular arc.
Collisions effectively calculate the value of Pi.

Planned animations:
Summarize the mapping between physics and Pi.
Display final result formula in #FFFFFF.
Fade out with clear closing visual.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = ["Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.", "The wall collision reverses the small block.", "Momentum and kinetic energy remain conserved."]
        self.setup_layout("The Setup: The Elastic Collision Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements

        block_M = Square(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.6)
        label_m = MathTex("m").next_to(block_m, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_M = MathTex("M=100m").next_to(block_M, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.place_at_grid(system, 'C3')
        self.add(system)

        self.play(block_m.animate.shift(LEFT * 1), run_time=1)
        self.play(Flash(block_m, color=RED, line_length=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Intuition", [
            "Counting collisions is measuring an angle.",
            "Discrete bounces approximate the circular arc.",
            "Collisions effectively calculate the value of Pi."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualizing angle vs collision
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        line = Line(start=circle.get_center(), end=circle.point_from_proportion(0.2), color=YELLOW)
        angle_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color=YELLOW)
        self.add(circle, line)
        self.place_at_grid(angle_label, 'B3')
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Discrete bounces arc
        arc = Arc(radius=1.5, angle=PI/3, color=RED, stroke_width=8)
        self.place_at_grid(arc, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Pi formula
        pi_formula = MathTex(r"\pi \approx \sum \text{collisions}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Write(pi_formula))
        self.wait(2)
